title: Can a correct key fail under the wrong alignment rule?
question: How do rigid and skip-aware decoders recover known rune sequences under four declared encoder mechanisms?
summary: Planted controls separate exact rune recovery, permitted alignments, beam pruning and English score acceptance across 216 plants and 2160 decoder results.

scope.representation: First min(240, available) output rune indices from all nine known-reading traces; canonical GP labels only for scoring.
scope.procedure: Plant ordinary addition, probabilistic collision skipping, value rewriting and one unrelated advance plus skipping; decode with correct/wrong deterministic key fixtures using rigid subtraction and four bounded beams.
scope.parameters: Nine traces, three seeds, key-value repetitions 1 and 4, 10000 slots; beam widths 16/64 crossed with skip limits 1/3; cumulative quadgram selection, normalized acceptance -5.5; 216 plants and 2160 decoder results.
scope.exclusions: No manuscript cipher identification, general recovery guarantee, language identification, uniform-pad assumption, key search or calibrated false-positive probability.

finding: Correct-key ordinary addition recovers exactly throughout. Skip limits exclude some true alignments; a wider beam cannot repair them. Rewriting often passes the language threshold without exact rune recovery. All wrong-key controls fail exact recovery and the threshold.
limitations: Artificial encoders and dependent known-text controls, not a fitted manuscript model. Exact alignment and exact plaintext are distinct. Cumulative and normalized scores have different objectives. Human review pending.
next_steps: Test newly declared alignment mechanisms as separate variants; calibrate best scores from complete bounded wrong-key searches.

family.title: Decoder alignment controls
family.question: Can declared decoders recover planted plaintext under matching and mismatched alignment rules?

variant.label: Four encoders with fixed rigid and beam decoders

review.reviewer: Codex; independent encoder, candidate and beam replay; human review pending
